text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy challenged former president Kenneth Kaunda to explain discussions he held with South Africa's leading arms manufacturers, Armscor. It said the talks, which followed predictions of civil strife by Kaunda, were suspicious.

- Twelve opposition parties said they were willing to resume dialogue with the government, provided talks focused on repealing the 1996 constitution, annulling last year's election results and the creation of an interim government.
- The Lusaka Stock Exchange forecast a 24 percent rise in inflation following a 24 percent increase in fuel prices.
- The mine workers' union calls for the speedy privatisation of coal producer Maamba Collieries.
- Zambian and Kenyan government officials are expected to meet on June 24 in Nairobi to resolve business conflicts between their respective airlines.
- The ruling party's Lusaka province chairman urged president Frederick Chiluba to declare a state of emergency to allow the government to deal with opposition parties calling for war.
- Leader of the opposition Liberal Progressive Front Rodger Chongwe said he was poisoned at a Zimbabwe hotel at the weekend.
- Opposition leaders urged judges to reject generous pay increases awarded to them by the government, saying these were meant to compromise their independence.
